clue.text: Tailor mostly cut widow's garments and woollen clothes

indicators.note: with most of the word cut away, only its opening letter survives

parts.note: the word with all but its first letter cut
widow's weeds are the black mourning clothes of a widow

explanation.surface: A tailor trims a widow's mourning outfit and some woollen garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweeds are suits or garments made from tweed, a rough woven wool cloth.

clue.text: Storm ripped over part of Colorado

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits over, i.e. above, the next
only a portion of the following word is wanted, its tail end here

parts.note: the last three letters of the state name

explanation.surface: A storm tore across part of the American state of Colorado.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating windstorm, a kind of storm.

clue.text: Price is less than seven shillings

indicators.note: what is wanted is less than the full phrase, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: Something costs under seven shillings, an old British sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: Price here is a bookmaker's price, the betting odds on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Evens is the betting price at which a winning bet pays the same amount as the stake.

clue.text: See AIDS treated as illness

indicators.note: something treated is processed and altered, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor regards AIDS as an illness to be treated.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease is a disorder of the body, a straightforward synonym for an illness.

clue.text: Basket contains heads of political undesirables: nobs and nobles get beheaded

indicators.note: a word that is beheaded loses its first letter
the heads of words are their first letters

parts.note: first letters of these three words
the word with its head removed

explanation.surface: A revolutionary scene where the toffs and aristocrats are guillotined and their heads go in a basket.
explanation.walkthrough: The heads of four words come first; then 'get beheaded' is read as an instruction applied to the word get itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A punnet is a small square basket or container used for selling soft fruit.

clue.text: Cheerful over strike

parts.note: time is up when it is over

explanation.surface: Workers are cheerful now the industrial action is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbeat describes an optimistic, positive mood, a synonym for cheerful.

clue.text: Non-union employees were originally fair game

indicators.note: the origin of each word is its first letter

parts.note: first letters of the three words, the hyphenated one counting once

explanation.surface: Workers outside the union were once considered legitimate targets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair game' looks like one phrase, but fair gives a piece and game alone is the definition. Newmarket is also a Suffolk horse-racing town.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket is a card game in which players lay cards in sequence, betting on certain cards.

clue.text: Time ran out for novelist

indicators.note: letters put out of place are disordered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer missed a deadline: the time allowed has run out.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose Tremain is an English writer of novels such as Restoration.

clue.text: Decoration makes woman angry

explanation.surface: Someone's choice of ornament annoys a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victoria Cross is Britain's highest military medal for gallantry, a decoration in the honours sense.

clue.text: Box, maybe, found in street

indicators.note: the letters are discovered lying inside the next word

explanation.surface: A cardboard box has been left lying in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Box is not a container here but the evergreen shrub used for hedging; 'maybe' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Box is a small evergreen shrub or tree, an example of the category.

clue.text: Produce silk hat for Shane Warne, perhaps

parts.note: a bowler is a hard round felt hat

explanation.surface: Making a silk hat as a gift for the Australian cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: Shane Warne was a famous Australian cricketer who bowled leg-spin, making the ball turn off the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Warne is an example of a cricketer whose deliveries rely on spin rather than pace.

clue.text: Revulsion and ecstasy in dodgy sauna

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the middle of another
something dodgy is unsound, so these letters are unreliable and get rearranged

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Drug-taking in a seedy sauna provokes disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea is a feeling of sickness, extended to strong disgust or loathing.

clue.text: Reckless youth gets injury on holiday

parts.note: a tear is a rip, as in a muscle

explanation.surface: A wild teenager hurts himself while on vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearaway is a wild, impetuous young person who behaves rashly.

clue.text: Fathers for Justice finally produces

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: to bear fruit or young is to produce it

explanation.surface: The campaign group Fathers 4 Justice at last brings something forth.
explanation.walkthrough: Fathers 4 Justice is a British fathers' rights campaign group, known for stunts in superhero costumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Forebears are ancestors, the fathers of earlier generations.

clue.text: First of salmon are up the Mobile River

indicators.note: mobile letters move about freely into a new order
the first letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: letters to rearrange along with the one above

explanation.surface: Salmon swimming upstream, apparently up the Mobile River in Alabama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Mobile River' reads as a real US river; Mobile is the anagram signal and River the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Euphrates is a major river of western Asia, flowing through Turkey, Syria and Iraq.

clue.text: Alaska and Indiana are alike

parts.note: the US postal abbreviation for Alaska
the US postal abbreviation for Indiana

explanation.surface: Two American states are said to be similar.
explanation.definitionFit: Akin means of similar character, a close synonym for alike.

clue.text: What Eminem does to get hits

definitions.meaning: first meaning: performs rap music, as the American rapper does
second meaning: sharp knocks or blows

explanation.surface: How the rapper Eminem achieves chart success.
explanation.walkthrough: Hits suggests chart hits, but it means blows.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both performs rhythmic spoken lyrics and sharp blows or knocks.

clue.text: Excellent, if not initially exciting

indicators.note: the word is used without its opening letter

explanation.surface: Something is first-rate, provided it is thrilling.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripping is dated British slang for splendid or first-rate.

clue.text: Girls fit in well in Kent

definitions.note: the answer is a town in Kent rather than a synonym for the phrase

parts.note: maids are girls or young women
to tone in is to blend or harmonise

explanation.surface: Young women settle in nicely in the English county of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidstone is the county town of Kent, so the clue locates it rather than defining it.

clue.text: Red, dead, revolutionary — and feared!

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A dead communist revolutionary who was much feared.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreaded means regarded with great fear or apprehension.

clue.text: Start to navigate Dart's less broad stretches

indicators.note: the start of the following word, its first letter

parts.note: darts are small arrows thrown at a board

explanation.surface: Steering a boat along the tighter reaches of Devon's River Dart.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dart is a river in Devon, which makes the surface read as navigation; here it means the missile thrown in darts.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrows are the slender stretches of a river or sea passage where it is less wide.

clue.text: Heathen emperor's private goddess

indicators.note: what is private is kept within, so the letters lie inside the words

explanation.surface: A pagan ruler worships his own personal deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Athene, or Athena, is the Greek goddess of wisdom and war.

clue.text: A canny type, Macbeth perhaps has to take on king

indicators.note: taking something on means adding it to the end of what is already there

parts.note: Verdi wrote an opera of Macbeth
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's scheming Macbeth must seize the throne from the king.
explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth suggests the play or its hero, but Verdi's opera version is what is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: An operator is a shrewd, skilful person, as in a smooth operator.

clue.text: Bush's authority figures

definitions.note: read as bushes, a plural noun
definitions.meaning: first meaning: shrubs of the genus bearing elderberries
second meaning: senior members of a church or community

explanation.surface: President Bush's senior advisers.
explanation.walkthrough: Bush looks like the American president; it is the plant, with 's read as making a plural.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both elderberry shrubs and senior people who hold authority in a group.

clue.text: Andy Warhol finally managed to become a superstar

indicators.note: letters that are managed are handled and arranged differently
finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Andy Warhol eventually achieved superstar fame.
explanation.walkthrough: Warhol coined 'superstars' for his circle; here the superstar is Bob Dylan, the singer-songwriter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Dylan is a hugely famous American singer-songwriter, an example of a superstar.

clue.text: Girl got worked up and upset

parts.note: short for the girl's name Diana

explanation.surface: A girl became agitated and unhappy.
explanation.definitionFit: Distressed means suffering anxiety or sorrow, a synonym for upset.

clue.text: Only Nonconformist in French city

indicators.note: a nonconformist refuses the usual order, so the letters break their arrangement

explanation.surface: The sole Protestant dissenter living in a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: Nonconformist with a capital looks like a religious dissenter outside the Church of England; here it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyon is the major city in east-central France, at the meeting of the Rhône and Saône.

clue.text: Well, he does go over the top

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an oil well whose oil spurts out unchecked

definitions.text: he does go over the top
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an effusive person who praises too much

explanation.surface: A shrug at a man who always exaggerates.
explanation.walkthrough: Well looks like a throat-clearing interjection, but it is the noun, an oil well.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a spouting oil well and someone who is overly effusive.

clue.text: Vacuous airhead sadly is no beauty

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word is emptied of its middle letters
things that go sadly go wrong, so the letters fall out of order

explanation.surface: The empty-headed person, unfortunately, is not good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis, the handsome youth of Greek myth, names any strikingly good-looking young man.
